turns.question: At which hour of the day were the most page views recorded between 20 September and 3 October 2026, and how many page views were in that hour?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no metric by hour of the day: page views are counted per day at the finest, so I cannot give the peak hour; the closest metrics are Site sessions (site_sessions, sessions with a page view, by day) and Customer actions (customer_actions filtered to the page_view action type, by day).

turns.question: What was the median time in hours between an outreach message and the partner's reply, for messages sent between 1 and 3 October 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no metric for the time between an outreach message and its reply, median or otherwise; the closest metrics are Messages sent (messages_sent), Messages replied (messages_replied), Replies (replies) and Reply rate (reply_rate).

turns.question: What share of candidates who applied in September 2026 reached the interview stage or beyond?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no metric for the share of applicants who reached a hiring stage; the closest metrics are Applications (applications, candidates who applied, on the day they applied) and Candidates in stage (candidates_in_stage, which can be filtered on the hiring stage and the applied date).

turns.question: What was the median number of days from application to hire for candidates hired in September or October 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no median time-to-hire metric; the one definition of time to hire is Time to hire (days) (time_to_hire_days), which is an average: "Average days from applying to being hired over the candidates hired in the period asked, on the day they were hired", and Hires (hires) is the other closest metric.

turns.question: How many degrees Celsius warmer was Istanbul than Amsterdam on average in daily temperature on 1 and 2 October 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no temperature or weather metric, so I cannot answer this; its closest metrics are about the shop's own data, for example Revenue (EUR) or Orders by customer country (TR, NL), which say nothing about temperature.

turns.question: What was the total ad spend in EUR per non-cancelled order placed in September 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no ad spend per order metric; the closest metrics are Ad spend (EUR) (ad_spend_eur), Orders (orders_total, filterable to non-cancelled statuses) and Cost per booking (EUR) (cost_per_booking_eur), the one definition of cost per conversion, which divides spend by bookings, not orders.

turns.question: How many delivery-topic customer service calls were there per 100 shipped orders in September 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no metric for calls per 100 shipped orders; the closest metrics are Calls labelled (calls_labelled, by the model-derived call__topic) and Orders (orders_total, filtered to order status shipped).

turns.question: What was the median order amount in EUR for non-cancelled orders placed in September 2026?
turns.answer: Median order value (EUR) (median_order_value_eur) exists only on the BigQuery warehouse and is not available here, so the semantic layer here has no median order amount metric; the closest metric is Average order value (EUR) (average_order_value_eur), the average amount of a non-cancelled order.

turns.question: What was the 90th percentile order amount in EUR for all orders placed between 17 August and 2 October 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no percentile order amount metric; the closest metrics are Average order value (EUR) (average_order_value_eur) and Orders (orders_total), which can be filtered on the order amount (for example orders over a given amount).

turns.question: How many customers placed more than three orders between 17 August and 2 October 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no metric for customers with more than three orders; the closest metrics are Repeat customers (repeat_customers, customers with two or more orders in all) and Active customers (customers_distinct, distinct customers with at least one non-cancelled order).

turns.question: For customers whose first order was placed in October 2026, what was the median number of days between their signup date and that first order?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no metric for the days between signup and first order; the closest metrics are Signup-to-first-order rate (signup_to_first_order_rate, the share of customers who ordered within 30 days of signing up) and Signups (signups).

turns.question: Between 17 August and 10 October 2026, how much higher in EUR was the average non-cancelled order amount of customers who signed up before 2026 than that of customers who signed up in 2026?
turns.answer: From 17 August to 10 October 2026, Average order value (EUR) was 102.67 EUR for customers who signed up before 2026 (all of them signed up in 2024) and 41.00 EUR for customers who signed up in 2026; the semantic layer has no metric for the difference between the two, so I give each figure under its metric's label.
